steps.text: It's high autumn.

The courtyard is silent. Its long, thick walls prevent outside noise from coming in. It's empty, save for an old persimmon tree leaning against the wall in the shade, with its old crown extending over the top of the wall.
No one knows what this old tree has witnessed over the years. We do know that, since its planting, it has turned red, and green, and red again, as the seasons have flown by.
Each year, bright red, fresh persimmons grow from its branches, and each year, these beautiful fruits wipe away old memories of previous harvests.
The old man sits under the tree, sleeping in the shade.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: ...Grandfather.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Grandfather?

steps.name: Kind Old Man
steps.text: Huh.... wha?

steps.name: Kind Old Man
steps.text: Ciqiu? You're back?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Yes. I got delayed a bit on the way back, but thankfully, I made it in time for the Mid-Autumn festival.

steps.name: Kind Old Man
steps.text: I've been thinking a lot these past few days. I've been watching the persimmons grow redder and redder. I was afraid that if you didn't come back soon, we wouldn't be able to eat them together this year.

steps.name: Kind Old Man
steps.text: I'm not sure how many more harvests I will live to see. If you had come back any later, you may not have even seen me here...

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Grandfather...
Ning Ciqiu decides not to crack any jokes, as she usually would have done. She looks at the old man closely. He seems to have a few new wrinkles on his forehead this time.
The autumn wind blows suddenly, ruffling the old man's hair.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: We completed our trial of Dahuang's first mobile plate last month. I've finished up my work at the Ministry of Rites for now, so they allowed me two weeks' vacation.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You've worked really hard.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I heard about the goings-on in Dahuang as soon as they happened. I've detailed all my criticisms in my letters.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I know you were involved in the disaster relief effort as well, but every Yanese mandarin is duty-bound to protect the people. As an Assistant Minister of the Ministry of Rites, you must take responsibility for the poor management here.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Deducting half a year's pay is letting you off easy. You have nothing to complain about.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Of course I shall not complain, and I take my errors to heart.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Ciqiu, you must remember: do not focus on what you've already done; focus on what you still haven't done yet.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: As a magistrate, you must carry out the orders of your superiors, while winning over and maintaining the trust of those below you, the citizens.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: In your position, everything you do is only what was expected of you in the first place. However, should you fail in even the slightest of your responsibilities, it would be an unforgivable transgression.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: If you do not understand this, you are not fit to wear your magisterial robes.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: 'Devote all your energy to the cause, as that is all you have to give.' I still remember the words you taught me so many moons ago.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I shall take this mistake to heart, but I shan't despair. Quitting now would really be shirking my responsibilities.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Okay. I've said enough on this for now. I am not in your position, nor do I work in the Ministry of Rites. Therefore, I have no right to interfere.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Now, I am more worried about your injury. Are you well?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Do not worry, Grandfather. I recovered quite some time ago.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Broken bones take at least three months to heal, so please take caution. In a few days, after you get settled, make the time to go see a doctor. An old friend of mine gave me medicine patches. I'll give you some to take back home with you.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Very well, Grandfather.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You kids are always making me worry.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I'm just about to move back to my old hometown. My son and daughter never come to see me, and your sister is never home. Everyone's forgotten me.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: What you say about my sister sounds true, but as far as you being forgotten... forgive me, but these past few days you've closed your door to all visitors.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Ugh. This again? Kids these days, you don't have your priorities straight, do you?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I haven't had a single moment of peace in this courtyard since the beginning of last month.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The youth today are clever, dare not knock on my door to offer me wine or tea. Instead, they've started watering my flowers. My poor hydrangeas. I spent so long growing them, and these kids have already drowned three pots this year!

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Gah...

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: You've had so many visitors lately. I'd wager the Minister came and showed you the draft guest list of the Feast, didn't he?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: It's rare to see the True Lung even once a year. I'm sure many would treasure the chance to learn the latest court gossip.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I have no reason to meet the young lad. He's the Minister, after all. What does he need my input for?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Come now, Grandfather. You served for decades in the Ministry of Rites. Your achievements were many, and your legacy is secure.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: That's all in the past. If we keep focusing on the past, how will we deal with the present?

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: Mr. Ning, you have a guest.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I told you, no visitors. Who is it, anyways?

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: He says he is the Advisor of Yumen.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Hmm...?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The Advisor of Yumen? Never heard of him...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I don't care who he is. I said no visitors, and I meant it.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Grandfather, wait a moment. Might the advisor be here to see me?

steps.name: Ning's Servant
steps.text: Good sir, our master is not accepting visitors right now. Please come back another time.

steps.name: Ineloquent Man
steps.text: Please tell Ning, err, your master, that an old friend is here.

steps.name: Ning's Servant
steps.text: Sir, no offense... but judging by your age, are you sure you're an 'old friend' of the master's?

steps.name: Ineloquent Man
steps.text: It's true. I dare not make up stories.

steps.name: Ning's Servant
steps.text: Sir, please, be on your way. The master is not accepting any guests right now. If you really are an 'old friend', then I'm sure you wouldn't want to cause trouble, would you?
Mr. Liang...?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Do you not recognize me?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning! It's been a while...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I heard you just returned to Baizao. I wanted to see you.
Liang Xun's eyes shift from Miss Ning to the figure standing behind her, the kindly old man.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Don't just stand there, Ciqiu. Invite your friend in for a bit.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: What's the matter? Why isn't anyone eating?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Haha. I feel like the third wheel here, and an old one at that. Maybe I'll just step away for a moment, and the two of you can enjoy your meal?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No, no. You've got it all wrong. It's us young kids who are intruding on your magisterial greatness.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Grandfather, don't scare him like that.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahaha. I'm only kidding, Liang Xun, I assure you.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: When Ciqiu was still in Shangshu, she used to write me letters, talking about a magistrate there who was both supremely talented and dedicated to his people. Today, I finally got to meet him.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: When did I—

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahaha. It's my birthday in three days. I wasn't planning to go through the trouble of organizing a grand party or anything.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: So today, eating dinner and chatting with you two youths is how I will celebrate my birthday.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Let us wish many more years of health and life to your greatness.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Hear hear, Grandfather. Many happy returns.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Alright, alright. Enough of that. Let's eat.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Liang Xun, I thought you were a magistrate from Shangshu. Why have I now heard you are the Advisor of Yumen?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: And why have you traveled from Yumen all the way to Baizao?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Yumen's journey was a long one, and the people once living in Yumen have been resettled in batches in different nomadic cities along the route as planned. The last group settled down in Baizao a few days ago.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Wasn't Yumen patrolling the northwestern corridor? How did you end up all the way over here in Baizao?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Dear Grandfather, have you forgotten? Yumen changed its route at the beginning of this year. The new route it was traveling on took it right to Baizao.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: As for why Yumen traveled to Baizao, surely you remember that?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Ah... yes... because of that same old problem again.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: All those years of fighting, and still no resolution. It's been so long since I retired, and sometimes I still hear those voices in my nightmares. It gives me a headache.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It's a problem that's existed for several millennia now.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Sometimes, issues resolve with the passage of time. Other times, they get worse.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Now I think we need to find a way to solve it. Grandfather, do you have any ideas?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Me? Of course not. If I were to try and intervene, people would accuse me of being a dictator.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Not necessarily. The Minister has been coming to see you ever few days or so. He never mentioned this to you?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning, there are some things which your grandfather must keep private, you know.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahahaha. My granddaughter sure is direct. That's for sure.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: No matter. I am an ordinary citizen now. I am free to speak as I please without fear of divulging secrets, because I do not know any secrets. As for this matter, however, I must defer to the advice of the young.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Well, Liang Xun, what's your solution?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I dare not propose any grand solution. However, there is one thing I do know.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The best strategy is to disrupt your enemy's strategy.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: From the court's perspective, war has no upsides, only downsides. From the peoples' perspective, war means death and destruction.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: 'The best strategy is to disrupt your enemy's strategy.' That makes sense.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: But if we always followed this reasoning, the True Lung would not have started 'The Great Hunt' one thousand years ago, and Yan would never have experienced a millennium of prosperity.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Times change, and circumstances change. It's hard to compare things across different historical eras.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: That war a thousand years ago was called 'The Great Hunt', but it wasn't really a hunt. It was the Yanese people wresting their future from the hands of the 'gods'. Retreating, even just a little bit, would have resulted in their extinction.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: However, things are different now. We are operating from a place of strength. We can and must avoid war at all costs. We cannot allow our soldiers and civilians to suffer any further.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahaha. Very well said, young man! You are far more skilled than I ever was, that's for sure.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Goodness no! Forgive me for being so bold, your magisterial greatness.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You say war should be avoided, and I agree. Well then, surely you have an alternate strategy, right? A way to get the situation under control?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: Mr. Ning, another visitor has arrived.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: What's this now?

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: She says she is a deputy minister from the Judicial Review Office with urgent business to discuss with you. She insists on coming in.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: The Judicial Review Office?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I suppose I will have to let her in.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: My sincerest apologies, but I must excuse myself for a moment.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Ciqiu, please continue chatting with our guest here.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: A deputy minister? You don't think it's... Lin Qingyan, do you?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: You know her too?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Anyone who deals with the Tianshi Bureaus has at least heard of her.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: I've heard Bai Dingshan, the Bluethunder Count, is senior to her Shifu. She's skilled in Lei Fa and solves cases as quick as lightning.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: But I am not sure why she has come to see my grandfather...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You waited until I was asleep and then locked me in this room! Why?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm not a three-year-old, you know!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Let me out of here!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Dammit! I'm supposed to meet that lady now. I didn't even get her contact, so I can't call her. What am I gonna do?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No. I can't break the door down. They might kick me out of here, and then I'd have no place to stay.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But this window...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm on the eighteenth floor, huh? That's not THAT high. Alright. I'll jump!

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: Miss, you've been standing here for ages. Are you going to make a purchase, or not?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Sir, let me ask you again—this painting here, 'Springtime in the Garden', is it truly an original work by Shujiang?

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: Miss, you can ask anyone around here. They all know my shop only sells authentic goods. I certainly know how to spot a fake painting.

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: Look at the technique, the essence of the painting. Who else but Shujiang could have done that?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: I'm no art expert, but I see a serious anachronism in this painting.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: These grapes on the table here, this particular variety of grapes was not introduced from Gaul into Yan until the year 628. However, this painting is from the year 580. How do you explain that?

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: Oh come on. That's quite a nit to pick, isn't it? You're just trying to bargain down the price, aren't you?

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: I've seen your type so many times before. I'm warning you. You won't like me when I'm angry.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Good sir, I never intended to buy your painting in the first place. Why would I be trying to bargain with you?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Besides, what I said about the grapes is true. Don't take my word for it. Look it up, if you don't believe me.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: If you think I'm wrong, then prove it. Get as angry as you want; it won't turn your fake painting into a real one.

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: If you don't want to buy it, then why are you standing here?!

steps.name: Antique Shop Owner
steps.text: I swear to you, if I'm selling any fakes in this shop, may Heaven strike me down where I stand!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Why is there a canopy above the upper floor?

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: Blaze? How did you—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Ha... haha... I...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm not late, am I?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Sorry for making you wait. I've had so many guests visiting lately. Apologies.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You are...?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: My name is Lin Qingyan. I am a deputy minister with the Judicial Review Office. I came here to ask you a few questions, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The Judicial Review Office, you say? I haven't talked to anyone there in many, many years. I'm not even sure who's in charge there anymore. Is it Yu Cheng?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yu Cheng...? No. I'm afraid you're mistaken. Deputy Minister Yu is no longer working with us.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Ah, that's right. Now I remember. One of the Bluethunder Count's Lei Fa students transferred from the Tianshi Bureaus to the Judicial Review Office. Well, that must be you, yes?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I heard that Tianshi Bai was transferred back to Baizao a while ago, yet he still hasn't come to see me, not even for some tea or a bite to eat. I guess he doesn't have time for this old retiree.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: These are extraordinary times we are living in. The Tianshi Bureaus must be extremely busy. I'll mention it the Count the next time I see him.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Haha. Sorry for going off on a tangent there. Please, sit down and have some tea.
They sit down in an elegant room that's tastefully decorated and furnished. There seems to be an empty space on the wall where a painting should be hanging.
The part of the wall that had once been covered by the painting is a slightly different color, which makes it stick out even more.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Mr. Ning, the tea is elegant, and so are you. Everything in this room is excellent, but something's missing... a painting, perhaps?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yes. The missing painting is, in fact, a 'longevity painting' that someone gave me many years ago.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: It's supposed to help you live longer. But as the saying goes, the older you grow, the heavier birthdays feel. I believe it's served its purpose.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I would not have expected you to be superstitious, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Growing old has left me at fate's mercy, hardly free to act as I wish. It must make you laugh, yes?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But I heard that a thief tampered with one of your paintings recently.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: They 'sealed the lips' of the painting with honey. It's an old folk custom to celebrate the New Year. They do this in hopes that the Stove God 'will only say good things and not bad things'. Whoever the thief was, they had some other motive in mind besides theft.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Why did you not report this vandalism?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: If I never reported it, then how do you know about it?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: One of my colleagues is handling this case. I saw the case file. But the one who first reported it... I don't believe was anyone from your estate...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Well, I'm glad there's at least someone out there who cares about an old man like me.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I would not have expected you to believe in those folk tales, Deputy Minister Lin.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Haha. I am a mere citizen. You, on the other hand, are a mandarin, and your time is valuable. You came here today to ask me something. Just go ahead and ask me directly, please.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I came here to ask you about someone, not something.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Do you remember an individual named Gu Quan?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Grkh...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Ten years ago, Gu Quan accompanied some Yanese dignitaries on an official visit to Victoria. They encountered a Catastrophe, a blizzard, along the way, and poor Gu drowned in a river.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Have you any memory of that, Mr. Ning?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yes. How could I forget?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I believe it was December. It definitely happened in the winter. By the time the news reached Baizao, it was almost the new year.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I remember the Messenger told us that, after the storm came in, the envoys got trapped on the mountain. Gu Quan stayed at the back of the line, helping shepherd everyone else across the river. In the end, he's the one who ended up falling in.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Sigh. The river must have been freezing cold!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: It looks like that incident made quite an impact on you.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Gu Quan was a very good worker. He served the Ministry very well. He was very well-read and had excellent calligraphy.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: It's a pity he had no family. The only remnant of him is a cenotaph in Cemetery of the Virtuous. Every year, the Ministry of Rites sends someone to tend it and pay their respects...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: No family?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Look at me, blathering on again. Well, anyway, why do you mention Gu Quan?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: A Yanese diplomat dying in a foreign country... that is a major international incident. According to the Laws of Yan, both Yan and the other country must send experts to conduct a joint investigation and compile a final report.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: However, after Gu Quan's death, the Ministry of Rites did no such thing. Even more startling is that the Judicial Review Office's records of the case are remarkably sparse.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I'm confused. This is clearly a question for the Judicial Review Office. Why are you asking me? I was in the Ministry of Rites.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Well then, let me remind you.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Two months before the team left on their mission, Gu Quan was just an ordinary ninth-rank mandarin. How did he suddenly get promoted to envoy, much less be sent on a mission to Victoria?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Well, you are the one who signed Gu Quan's transfer order. At the time, you were the Minister of Rites.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahaha. Now I understand.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You're saying that I deliberately arranged for Gu Quan to go on a diplomatic mission to Victoria, and then 'disposed' of him.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: No. That's not what I'm saying.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: There is something strange going on here. I intend to solve these cases one-by-one, and I humbly ask for your guidance, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Since you're so curious about all this, why not ask me a few more pointed questions?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Do you think it's odd that I, as a former Minister of Rites, would trouble myself over a mere ninth-rank ceremonial officer? Are you implying, perhaps, that he discovered some unspeakable secret about me?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: So you're just here to ask me about a ten year old case?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahaha... no matter, no matter. Ask whatever you wish.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Just remember, if you keep asking the same questions, you will keep getting the same answers.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: What kind of answers do you want?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Truthful ones.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahaha. I already have one foot in the grave. What reason do I have to deceive you?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Then again, if you suspect me of committing so many crimes, then you surely don't view my testimony as credible...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I just want you to tell me why Gu Quan was suddenly transferred. Once you tell me that, we'll be able to figure out the rest of it.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Okay, okay. You came all this way to see me, so I think I should tell you what you want to know.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Gu Quan was indeed transferred for a reason: because he specifically requested it.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: He wanted the transfer?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yes, he said that he was ill and was afraid he didn't have much time left, so he wanted to return to his hometown in Victoria to live out the rest of his days. So, I agreed to let him join the delegation to Victoria.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What illness did he have?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I'm not clear on the details either. I only vaguely remember that Gu Quan did seem to be in poor spirits around that time.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But, as such a low-level mandarin, Gu Quan would not have had many opportunities to even meet you. How did he make such a request?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: To be honest, it's a bit embarrassing... but there was a hint of selfishness on my part as well.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Gu Quan had magnificent penmanship, so I sometimes had him write letters for me. I also asked him to serve as my children's calligraphy tutor.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: He had done so much for me, I felt I owed him a favor. Besides, I did not feel his request stemmed from greed.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: That's all there is to say about Gu Quan's transfer. Do you have any other questions for me?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Since I've heard it directly from you, I'll take what you're saying at face value.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: However, I disagree with one thing you said.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Anyone who wants to know the truth, be they a mandarin or an ordinary citizen, does not need a special reason for doing so.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Please know, Mr. Ning, that I am indeed only after the truth. I have no other motives.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Now I shall take my leave, sir.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Good day, madam.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Say. Where is Liang Xun?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: It's rather late, Grandfather. I saw the young man out many hours ago.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: My word. You invited him in to have dinner, and then you had him wait there forever. Tis a poor way to treat a guest.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yes. Where are my manners? Tell him I apologize, and please let him know that he's welcome to come back any time. Next time, I will be a proper host. I owe him that much.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Liang is a reasonable man. I am sure he'll understand.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: By the way, his name is Liang Xun, right? Which 'Xun' is that? How do you write it?

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: It's that Xun with three dots on the left.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Uh, that one in 'Xun mei qie yi'... A spray of spring, gifted to you. Such a beautiful name; I'm rather fond of it.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I've heard that people with the three dots in their name characters are as clever and swift as water.

steps.name: Ning Ciqiu
steps.text: Funny. The others all say he's as dull as a board.
The old man walks to the table, picks up a pen, and adds another name to the invite list.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hmm... maybe he is rather dull...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: He came all this way to see his 'sweetheart', but look at the gifts he brought: Yumen's Tea, some strange liquor called 'Liedaozi'. These seem more like gifts meant for me.
Lin Qingyan, wait.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Who's there?
Lin Qingyan gets a strange feeling she's rarely felt before.
A woman with a sword advances to within a zhang of Lin Qingyan, yet she doesn't even notice her...

of Lin Qingyan, yet she doesn't even notice her...

steps.text: Until she is standing right in front of her.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Your uniform...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You... you're... an Imperial Guard?
